beyond the suite: `once` mid-list, add-mid-emit not double-called, remove-mid-emit not skipping its neighbours, emit return counts, duplicate registrations, `prev` correctness for `sort`/`rename`/`remove` in sequence, caller-supplied `initial` never mutated, `replay` parity, sort idempotence.

One probe initially reported FAIL — that was my own expectation being wrong (I typo'd the `next` column on the rename case), not the code. Worth flagging so you don't read the sequence as a masked failure.

**Risk / the judgement call I made:** the README says removal mid-emit must not cause *any other* listener to be skipped or called twice. That's satisfiable by snapshot alone, but I implemented the stronger reading — an unsubscribe takes effect immediately, even mid-emit. If you actually want the frozen-set semantics (a listener removed during an emit still receives that one in-flight emit), delete the `if (!entry.live) continue;` line at `src/emitter.js:45`; the rest stands. Not checked: there are no other test files in the repo and no reference branch, so the visible suite is all the coverage that exists — nothing pins the mid-emit removal semantics either way.

Per your rules I haven't committed anything; `src/emitter.js` and `src/reducers.js` are modified in the working tree, `test/` untouched.Done — final state:

- **`src/emitter.js`** — listeners stored as `{ fn, live }` entries; `emit` walks a snapshot taken at the start of the emit, skipping entries unsubscribed before their turn. A `once` listener unsubscribing itself no longer shifts the loop past the next listener, and nothing added mid-emit gets called an extra time.
- **`src/reducers.js`** — `sort` copies first (`[...state.items].sort(byName)`), so `prev` handed to change listeners keeps the old order and undo restores the right thing.

`npm test` → 6/6 pass (was 4/6), plus 16 extra edge-case probes green. `test/store.test.js` untouched; nothing committed — the two modified files are yours to review and commit.
